strengths: Novel SAE feature coactivation method with practical efficiency—requires only a handful of prompts compared to full circuit tracing
Strong empirical results with high steering success rates (96% country, 92% relation, 90% composite), demonstrating genuine causal effects
Interesting and well-demonstrated finding of hierarchical organization: concrete entities in early layers, abstract relations in deeper layers
Composability discovery shows components can be combined to produce compound counterfactual outputs, suggesting genuine modularity
Context consistency findings (identical country components across relations, identical relation components across countries) are valuable
Clear presentation with effective visualizations, detailed methodology, and comprehensive reproducibility information
Well-described methods using publicly available models and tools with proper licensing
weaknesses: Severely limited evaluation scope: restricted to one task family (country-relation tasks) with only 10 countries—insufficient to support claims about general LLM modularity
Limited model coverage: primary evaluation on Gemma 2 2B only; 9B results show consistency but do not test other model families (GPT, Llama, Claude, etc.)
Unjustified hyperparameter choices: correlation threshold τ_corr=0.9, density threshold τ_density=0.01, and k=5 feature selection lack ablation studies or justification
No baseline or alternative method comparisons despite mentioning ACDC, path patching, and other circuit discovery approaches; unclear if graph construction adds value
Limited statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, no error analysis of 4-10% failure cases, imprecise reporting ('around 70 components'), no significance testing
Relies on pre-trained SAEs without validating quality, monosemanticity, or reconstruction fidelity; cannot use newer SAE architectures
Causal claims not fully justified: ablations during forward pass don't establish true causal mechanisms or directionality; distinction between necessary vs. sufficient conditions unclear
Component identification via weakly connected components is straightforward but arbitrary—no sensitivity analysis or comparison to alternatives like clustering or spectral methods
Feature interpretation limitations: Neuronpedia descriptions acknowledged as unreliable; limited human validation beyond automatic descriptions and ablation effects
High-density features produce incoherent outputs (noted in limitations) but are dismissed rather than investigated
Single prompt template for collection—robustness to paraphrasing unexplored; no investigation of when/why modularity emerges or generalization beyond factual knowledge tasks

strengths: Clear methodology and effective presentation of the pipeline from SAE activations to component steering
Reproducible work using publicly available SAEs with transparent hyperparameter documentation
Strong empirical steering results (90-96% success rates) across multiple prompt templates, suggesting some generalization within the task domain
Interesting finding about layer-wise distribution (concrete entities in early layers, abstract relations in later layers)
Validation on larger model (Gemma 2 9B) showing consistency of findings
weaknesses: Severely restricted scope: entire analysis limited to three relations (capital, currency, language) across 10 countries with no evidence of generalization to other domains or task types—claims about 'composable semantic modules' in LLMs rest on this narrow evidence

Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (standard SAEs, correlation-based graphs, density-based pruning, BFS) with only incremental improvements over prior coactivation analysis work
Methodological concerns: key hyperparameters (τ_corr=0.9, k=5, τ_density=0.01) lack justification or ablation studies; component definition appears post-hoc
Causal claims are overstated: ablation/amplification of SAE features is behavioral perturbation, not mechanistic causal intervention; no actual tracing of causal pathways

Semantic coherence not reliably demonstrated: paper admits feature descriptions (from GPT-4) sometimes fail to reflect extracted concepts; Spain components lack Spain mentions despite being labeled Spain components
Poor component extraction efficiency: ~70 components per task but only 2-3 show significant causal effects; leaves unexplained what remaining 67 components represent
Generalization claims unsupported: tests different templates but same task; no cross-domain or cross-task generalization; unexplained variance in success rates (Poland/Spain 78% vs others 100%)

Missing mechanistic insight: describes pattern (entities early, relations late) without explaining why or how components function; 'composability' framing oversold as mainly showing feature addition/subtraction
Lacks comparative evaluation: no comparison to alternative discovery methods (knowledge neurons, ACDC, etc.) or simpler baselines
Statistical rigor insufficient: small sample (10 countries), no error bars/confidence intervals, no ablation studies on design choices

strengths: Novel and computationally efficient method for discovering interpretable components via SAE feature coactivation, lighter than exhaustive circuit tracing approaches
Strong and consistent empirical results with high steering success rates (96% country, 92% relation, 90% composite) across 10 countries and 3 relations, replicated on two model sizes
Well-designed causal ablation experiments with clear evidence that component manipulation reliably alters model behavior, including compelling counterfactual steering demonstrations

Insightful finding of hierarchical organization: entity representations emerge in early layers while relational abstractions concentrate in later layers, with within-component analysis showing stronger causal effects from deeper nodes
Good reproducibility: open-source models, transparent hyperparameters, comprehensive license documentation, reliance on standard tools (TransformerLens, SAE Lens, NetworkX)
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: restricted entirely to country-relation factual knowledge tasks (3 relations, 10 countries); no demonstration on other semantic knowledge types or reasoning tasks despite claiming insights about LLM organization generally

Insufficient validation of 'semantic coherence' claim: relies on Neuronpedia descriptions (acknowledged as unreliable), post-hoc inspection, and ablation results; no explicit semantic similarity metrics or comparison to random baselines

Critical methodological gaps: correlation threshold (0.9), feature selection (k=5), and density threshold (0.01) lack principled justification or sensitivity analysis; high-density features dismissed despite producing incoherent outputs but merit investigation

Weak statistical rigor: success rates computed on small prompt sets without confidence intervals or significance testing; Appendix C shows notable variance (Poland/Russia at 50-78% for currency) not discussed; no per-component reliability analysis

Compositionality assumption inadequately tested: composite steering success (90%) notably lower than individual steering; no systematic analysis of composition failures or evidence that components can be independently manipulated without interaction

Limited generalization evidence: only two Gemma 2 models tested, no other architectures explored; claims of generalization unsupported; unclear if findings specific to factual recall or transfer to reasoning, generation, or abstract tasks

Incomplete analysis: no ablations on pruning strategy or architectural choices; no investigation of false positives among ~70 components per task; failure modes (e.g., Poland currency at 78%) unexplored; prompt dependence unclear despite different templates in evaluation

Network interpretability questionable: graph visualizations (Figures 3-4, 8-9) difficult to parse; no assessment of how many extracted components lack semantic meaning or analysis of feature interactions within components

strengths: Well-motivated approach to mechanistic interpretability using SAE feature coactivation that offers efficiency gains over exhaustive circuit tracing
Thorough experimental validation with multiple steering paradigms (concept, relation, composite) demonstrating causal effects through principled ablation/amplification
Valuable finding that concrete concepts emerge in early layers while abstract relations concentrate in later layers, aligning with hierarchical processing theories
Clear demonstration of compositionality: combining concept-relation components produces compound counterfactual outputs (e.g., steering to 'English')
Components substantially outperform single-feature baselines (e.g., 96% vs 83% for country facts composite steering)
Honest documentation of limitations and extensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Replication on Gemma 2 9B model shows consistency of core findings
weaknesses: Severely limited task scope: only 3 multi-relational reasoning tasks with small example counts; failed entirely on 3 additional tasks (Spanish conjugation, Nobel Prize facts, animal taxonomy) because model didn't achieve 100% accuracy, raising critical questions about applicability

Manual component selection undermines scalability claims: identification requires manual inspection of descriptions, empirical observation of ablation effects, and task-specific heuristics (intersection-based for country facts, union-based for translation, concept-relation specific for verbs)

Semantic coherence validation inadequate: relies on Neuronpedia descriptions which authors acknowledge are 'often unreliable' (Spain components don't mention Spain, 'beautiful' includes Scotland, language components described as 'programming'); no systematic quantification or human evaluation

Poor performance on complex reasoning: verb transformation composite ~22% average, synonym/antonym 0-2% (at baseline), word translation composite ~59% with some words at 5%—failures inadequately explained

Cross-task evaluation reveals fragility: ablating verb transformation components severely degrades accuracy on other tasks (73-66% for country facts, 64% for translation), suggesting components may be statistical artifacts rather than genuine modules

Hyperparameter choices insufficiently justified: correlation threshold 0.9, density threshold 0.01 (following 'Neuronpedia standard'), top-k=5 lack motivation; transcoder experiments required τ_corr=0.7, indicating parameter sensitivity without sensitivity analysis
Limited technical novelty: uses pre-trained SAEs, standard Pearson correlation for graphs, basic BFS for components; main contribution is application rather than methodological innovation

Insufficient failure mode analysis: some verbs show 6-20% steering success with claim of 'unstable components' but no investigation into why; speculation about sink components representing words beginning with 's' is unvalidated

Reproducibility concerns: depends on Neuronpedia pre-trained SAEs, manual component selection steps difficult to replicate, code availability not mentioned, would be challenging for others to extend to new tasks

Limited comparison to alternatives: only compared to single-feature baselines; no quantitative comparison to attention heads, other circuit discovery methods, or recent techniques (e.g., Marks et al. 2025)
Weak theoretical framing: primarily empirical analysis; no explanation for why this modular hierarchical organization emerges or formal analysis of compositionality properties
Fragility of 'modular organization' claims: the fact that components severely degrade cross-task performance suggests tight coupling rather than clean modularity

strengths: Interesting methodological combination of SAE coactivation patterns with network analysis and causal interventions
Comprehensive experimental reporting with extensive supplementary materials and detailed ablations
Clear presentation and effective visualizations (especially Figure 1, Figure 3) of the approach
Intriguing demonstrations of compositionality when combining concept and relation components
Well-organized appendices with task specifications, hyperparameters, and supplementary results supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only 3 simple factual/lexical tasks with minimal examples (10 countries, 11 words, 8 verbs); no evidence of generalization beyond these specific examples

Critical methodological flaw: component selection requires substantial manual intervention and task-specific heuristics (acknowledged by authors as requiring manual inspection and curation), contradicting claims of efficiency and scalability

Highly variable and inconsistent performance: steering success ranges from 0-100% across tasks (22-92% for composites, 26-93% for relations), with verb transformations near-random; within-task variance unexplained (e.g., possess 6% vs. like 83%)
Overstated causal claims: title and framing invoke 'causality' but the analysis is merely interventional (ablation/amplification); no true causal identification or counterfactual reasoning

Context-consistency claims contradicted by methods: components defined as intersections for some tasks but task-specific for others; this engineering suggests context-sensitivity rather than consistency

Weak experimental validation: only baseline is single-feature steering; no comparison to other mechanistic interpretability methods (circuits, knowledge neurons, attention heads); transcoder analysis achieves only 27% (relegated to appendix)

Numerous unjustified methodological choices without sensitivity analysis: correlation threshold τ_corr=0.9 (very high, no ablation), density threshold τ_density=0.01 (follows convention only), top-k=5 (no justification), steering strength selection via ad-hoc grid search

Limited model scale and generalization: primary results on Gemma 2 2B (very small model); 9B results in appendix; method fails on additional tasks (animal taxonomy); no evidence of scaling to larger models or complex reasoning
Dependency on pre-trained SAEs of acknowledged inconsistent quality; no ablation with alternative SAE architectures despite acknowledging improved variants exist

Absence of statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple-comparison corrections; small sample sizes; binary success metrics without analysis of near-misses or partial successes; no independent human evaluation of component semantics
Component semantics verified only through feature descriptions (acknowledged as unreliable) and ablation direction, creating confirmation bias risk in manual selection process

Missing critical ablations and analyses: no sensitivity studies, no investigation of component redundancy, no error analysis explaining massive variance in success rates, limited cross-task generalization testing
Failure to investigate causes of high variance: unexplained 6-83% range in steering success (Table 19) could indicate components don't robustly capture concepts, but this isn't analyzed

strengths: Rigorous causal validation: Comprehensive ablation and steering experiments with KL divergence measurement, context consistency analysis, and comparison to single-feature baselines demonstrate true causal effects rather than just correlation.

Well-motivated contribution: Addresses genuine interpretability gap by moving from individual features to compositional knowledge structures. Clear articulation of why global, sparse, feature-level interpretation is needed.

Compelling empirical findings: Demonstrates compositionality (combining concept + relation components yields interpretable compound effects), clear hierarchical organization (concrete entities early, abstract relations late), and practical steering success rates (48-96% concept, 26-93% relation steering).

Comprehensive experimental design: Multi-faceted evaluation across three diverse task types with analyses of layer distribution, compositionality, cross-task effects, and supplementary replication on larger model (Gemma 2 9B).

Exceptional presentation and reproducibility: Clear writing with effective visualizations, extensive appendices with full task specifications, prompts, hyperparameters, and supplementary results enabling reproducibility.
Honest limitation acknowledgment: Authors transparently discuss scope constraints, parameter choices, and failure modes rather than overclaiming generality.
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: Only 3 tasks with very small example counts (10 countries, 11 words, 8 verbs), primarily evaluated on Gemma 2 2B only. Attempted tasks failed (animal taxonomy, Spanish conjugation, Nobel Prize) raising questions about generalization to more complex reasoning, less compositional tasks, and out-of-distribution scenarios.

Manual and heuristic-driven component selection: Method requires manually inspecting feature descriptions and ablation results to identify 'semantically coherent' and 'compositional' components. This process limits scalability, introduces confirmation bias, makes application to new tasks unclear, and is acknowledged as bottleneck by authors but not resolved.

Substantial performance variability across relations: Concept steering ranges 48-96%, relation steering 26-93%, composite 22-92%. Notable failures on possess (6%), sink (20%), synonym/antonym (0%), capitalize tasks. Pattern suggests method is task-specific rather than general.

Polysemanticity undermines interpretability claims: Paper demonstrates SAE features remain polysemantic even within components (e.g., Scotland in 'beautiful' component). Components may similarly suffer—not all features contribute equally. Raises questions about whether component-level interpretation truly addresses polysemanticity problem.

Unjustified hyperparameter choices: Density threshold τ_density=0.01 and correlation threshold τ_corr=0.9 adopted without ablation. Appendix L shows τ_corr=0.7 works better for transcoders, suggesting these are model/task dependent. No systematic parameter sensitivity exploration.

Underdeveloped transcoder results: Appendix L shows only 27% steering success with transcoders vs. higher SAE rates, but relegated to appendix with minimal discussion. Why such large drop? What does this imply for method's generality to other interpretability tools?

Limited failure mode analysis: While failures noted (e.g., hide outputting all capitals, possess/sink instability), they aren't systematically investigated. Why do some relations fail to stabilize? What makes certain verbs resistant to steering?

Incomplete comparisons: Limited efficiency comparison to full circuit tracing (claimed lighter-weight but not quantified). No comparison to attention-head analysis or other module discovery approaches despite mentioning Todd et al. findings on antonym/past-tense.
